newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Clabecq steelworkers demonstrate in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Clabecq steelworkers demonstrate in Brussels.

text.p: About 300 workers from bankrupt steel firm Forges de Clabecq, their jobs on the line, demonstrated noisily but peacefully on Wednesday outside the Brussels office of Employment Minister Miet Smet.

Tossing firecrackers and a few eggs, chanting "Work: Yes, Unemployment: No" and refreshing themselves with soft drinks and sandwiches, the workers faced about 30 riot police and a water cannon across razor wire barricades.
A great cheer went up at one stage as a woman inside the building hung a sign declaring "Solidarity" from a third floor window and gave the crowd a thumbs up sign.

Union activist Roberto D'Orazio, who has led the fight to protect the steelworkers' jobs, met the minister and told the crowd she had promised to convene a meeting of the unions, the Walloon regional government and herself to examine the options.
Clabecq was declared bankrupt in January when the Walloon government, the biggest shareholder in the company, pulled the plug, threatening the jobs of the 1,800 workers.
Receivers, whose initial efforts to cobble together a rescue package failed when the main creditor banks refused to take part, are now focusing on finding a buyer for the firm as a going concern.
There have been several demonstrations by the Clabecq workers in Brussels and at the steel works itself near the town of Tubize about 30 km south of the Belgian capital.
On Sunday there will be another "March for Work" in Brussels including the workers from French carmaker Renault's doomed Belgian plant in Vilvoorde.

The French firm sparked a diplomatic row and fierce criticism when it announced two weeks ago without any warning that it would close the Vilvoorde plant in July with the loss of more than 3,000 jobs.
Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who lives in Vilvoorde, denounced the closure and the fact that it was announced without consulting the workers.

The European Commission said Renault had broken EU rules on worker consultation and the Belgian Federal and Flemish regional government said they would take the company to court. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6810
